title: From disc code to a running browser game
caption: Conceptual build and runtime flow, not a live compiler or a complete exported build recipe. Generated C++ preserves translated guest behavior. Browser execution still needs the runtime and access to the user's disc data.

steps.label: Disc
steps.title: Start with the game's executable inputs
steps.detail: Read the main ELF and the archive containing loaded modules. The disc also contains assets that are not executable code.

steps.label: Extract
steps.title: Identify the code that loads later
steps.detail: Extract the 325 MWo3 modules and record their load addresses and entry points. Translating the main ELF alone misses this code.

steps.label: Translate
steps.title: Translate guest instructions into C++
steps.detail: The recompiler emits C++ and dispatch tables. These are translated instructions, not the original developer's source.

steps.label: Build
steps.title: Link the translated code with the runtime
steps.detail: Emscripten builds the translated game and PS2 runtime into a matched web package: loader JavaScript, WebAssembly and packaged data.

steps.label: Run
steps.title: The player's browser executes the game
steps.detail: The local browser supplies graphics, audio and controller input. Runtime disc reads still need the user's game data; WASM alone is not the whole game.
